title: Filtered colimits of globally generated sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ its category of sheaves of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $S=\underline{\mathbf Z}$ for the constant abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For an abelian sheaf $G$, a global section is a compatible family $(s_U\in G(U))_{U\in\mathcal C}$ under every restriction map; equivalently it is a morphism $s:S\to G$. Say that $G$ is globally generated if the evaluation morphism
$$
 e_G:\bigoplus_{s\in\operatorname{Hom}(S,G)}S\longrightarrow G,
 \qquad e_G\circ j_s=s,
$$
is an epimorphism [def-galois-epi-final], where $j_s$ is the coproduct injection. This is the evaluation definition of [def-kun-global-generated] for abelian sheaves, written for a general site; on a site with a final object the compatible families are its global sections.

Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram in $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If every $F_i$ is globally generated, then the sheaf colimit $F=\varinjlim_{i\in I}F_i$ is globally generated.

proof.text: First check the general-site interpretation of global sections in the statement. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $S$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $\mathbf Z$. A compatible family $(s_U)$ defines a morphism from this presheaf to $G$ by $n\mapsto n s_U$ on $U$. Conversely any such presheaf morphism is determined by the images of $1$, which form a compatible family. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends it uniquely to $S\to G$. For a site with final object $T$, such families are uniquely obtained by restricting $s_T\in G(T)$. Thus on $T_{\Et}$ the evaluation above is exactly that of [def-kun-global-generated] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Statement: general-site meaning of global generation; comparison with the evaluation morphism used in ## Proof

proof.text: All small colimits in $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], using only its existence clause. In particular form $F$ with its cocone maps $c_i:F_i\to F$ and, for $G=F$ and every $G=F_i$, form $E_G=\bigoplus_{s:S\to G}S$. By the coproduct universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (a coproduct is a discrete colimit), the maps $s:S\to G$ define $e_G:E_G\to G$ with $e_Gj_s=s$. The hypothesis says that each $e_{F_i}$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves, (1); coproduct construction uses Categories Tag 002F, definition-colimit

proof.text:
For each $i$, define $h_i:E_{F_i}\to E_F$ by sending the summand indexed by $s:S\to F_i$ to the summand indexed by $c_i\circ s:S\to F$, using the identity on $S$. The coproduct universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] defines this map and gives
$$
 e_F\circ h_i=c_i\circ e_{F_i}:
 E_{F_i}\longrightarrow F,
$$
because both composites, after precomposition with the summand injection indexed by $s$, equal $c_i\circ s$.

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit, applied to discrete coproduct diagrams

proof.text:
To test whether $e_F$ is epi, take any abelian sheaf $H$ and maps $a,b:F\to H$ with $a\circ e_F=b\circ e_F$. Precompose this equality with $h_i$ and use step 3 to obtain
$$
 (a\circ c_i)\circ e_{F_i}=(b\circ c_i)\circ e_{F_i}.
$$
Since $e_{F_i}$ is epi, its right-cancellation property [def-galois-epi-final] yields $a\circ c_i=b\circ c_i$ for every $i$.

By the uniqueness clause in the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], two maps out of $F$ agreeing after every $c_i$ are equal: they are both factorizations of the same cocone $F_i\xrightarrow{a c_i}H$. Hence $a=b$. The definition [def-galois-epi-final] now says that $e_F$ is an epimorphism, which is exactly global generation in the statement. This proves the required filtered-colimit assertion; the cancellation argument does not require filteredness.

Made its global-generation meaning explicit by the same evaluation formula, using Hom from the constant integer sheaf to describe global sections without assuming a terminal site object. The imported proof uses geometric points of a scheme and so does not prove its general-site statement. Replaced it with five steps: identify global sections via sheafification, form evaluation maps, factor every stage evaluation through the colimit evaluation, cancel the stage epimorphisms, and apply colimit uniqueness. All needed facts already have DAG nodes, so no new nodes or Mathlib leaves were created.

lean.note: The evaluation helper belongs to the map explicitly introduced in this node, and extends the existing etale free-abelian-group model to arbitrary sites using Mathlib Sheaf.Γ and constantSheafΓAdj. Its source, the constant sheaf of the free abelian group on all global sections, is canonically the displayed coproduct of constant integer sheaves because constantSheaf is a left adjoint. Its adjoint linear-combination map sends each generator to the indexed section. No final object, stalks, arbitrary substitute map, extra existence hypotheses, or new global-generation predicate are used. Site object and morphism universes are independent; coefficients and the small diagram use their common maximum.
